---
title: Import from a URL
description: Have your ClipMux server fetch a video from a public URL and encode it, with no upload from your side.
---

When the file is already online, for example in another bucket or on your
old video host, your backend can hand ClipMux its URL. The server fetches
the file itself, stores it as the video's source and encodes it exactly as
it would an upload. Nothing passes through your backend or a browser.

## Before you start

- An API key with `assets:write`, from your backend.
- A URL that anyone on the internet can fetch with a plain `GET`: `http` or
  `https`, answering `200` with the file. A short-lived signed URL from your
  own storage works, as long as it lasts while the import runs.

## Import a video

<Tabs items={['Node', 'Python', 'Go', 'PHP']}>
<Tab value="Node">

```ts
import { ClipMux } from '@clipmux/node'

const clipmux = new ClipMux() // reads the CLIPMUX_* settings

const asset = await clipmux.assets.importUrl(
  {
    url: 'https://files.example.com/lesson-42.mp4',
    passthrough: 'lesson_42',
    title: 'Lesson 42: Sorting',
  },
  { idempotencyKey: 'import-lesson_42' },
)
console.log(asset.id, asset.status) // ast_… processing
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">

```python
import os, requests

res = requests.post(
    f"{os.environ['CLIPMUX_URL']}/v1/assets",
    headers={
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['CLIPMUX_API_KEY']}",
        "Idempotency-Key": "import-lesson_42",
    },
    json={
        "url": "https://files.example.com/lesson-42.mp4",
        "passthrough": "lesson_42",
        "title": "Lesson 42: Sorting",
    },
)
res.raise_for_status()
asset = res.json()  # status: processing
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="Go">

```go
body := strings.NewReader(`{"url": "https://files.example.com/lesson-42.mp4",
  "passthrough": "lesson_42", "title": "Lesson 42: Sorting"}`)
req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", os.Getenv("CLIPMUX_URL")+"/v1/assets", body)
req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+os.Getenv("CLIPMUX_API_KEY"))
req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
req.Header.Set("Idempotency-Key", "import-lesson_42")
res, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req) // 201: the asset, processing
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="PHP">

```php
$ch = curl_init(getenv('CLIPMUX_URL') . '/v1/assets');
curl_setopt_array($ch, [
    CURLOPT_POST => true,
    CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
    CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER => [
        'Authorization: Bearer ' . getenv('CLIPMUX_API_KEY'),
        'Content-Type: application/json',
        'Idempotency-Key: import-lesson_42',
    ],
    CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS => json_encode([
        'url' => 'https://files.example.com/lesson-42.mp4',
        'passthrough' => 'lesson_42',
        'title' => 'Lesson 42: Sorting',
    ]),
]);
$asset = json_decode(curl_exec($ch), true); // status: processing
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

`POST /v1/assets` answers `201` with the video, already `processing`, and
its playback IDs. With an `Idempotency-Key`, a retry of the same request
returns the same video instead of importing twice.

| Field | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | | The public `http` or `https` URL to fetch. Required. |
| `playback_policies` | `["signed"]` | One playback ID per policy: `signed` for a private video, `public` for one anyone with the URL can watch, or `["signed", "public"]` for both. |
| `passthrough` | | Your own ID for the video, up to 255 bytes. See [Link videos to your records](/docs/build/upload/passthrough). |
| `title` | | A name for people, one line, up to 200 characters. |
| `generate` | | `{ "subtitles": true, "chapters": true }` makes subtitles and chapters once the video is ready. Chapters imply subtitles. |
| `renditions` | every rung up to the source | The rungs to encode, for example `["1080p", "480p"]`. See [Choose renditions](/docs/build/upload/renditions). |

These are the same settings an upload takes: only `url` stands in for the
upload's `size`. When the video is ready, your webhook receives
`video.asset.ready`, as for an upload.

## From the dashboard or a terminal

In the dashboard, **Upload** takes a URL as well as files: paste it under
the drop zone, and the settings below apply to it as to a file.

From a terminal, give `clipmux push` (or `npx @clipmux/node upload`) the URL
in place of a file. Running the same command again creates nothing new:

```bash
CLIPMUX_API_KEY=cmx_… clipmux push --server https://video.example.com \
  --policy signed,public https://files.example.com/lesson-42.mp4
```

## What is refused

ClipMux fetches only public addresses, so an import can't be used to reach
the server's own machine or your private network. It refuses:

- a URL that isn't `http` or `https`, has no host, or is over 2048
  characters;
- a URL with credentials in it, such as `https://user:pass@…`;
- a host that is, or resolves to, a loopback, private, link-local or other
  non-public address, including cloud metadata addresses.

The address is checked on every connection, after DNS, and on each of up to
5 redirects, so a redirect or a DNS change can't lead around it. A URL that
is refused when you send it is `400 import_url_refused`, and nothing is
created. One that leads to a refused address later ends the video as
`errored` with `import_url_refused`.

## Sizes and failures

The file may be as large as an upload: `CLIPMUX_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` on the
server, or 312.5 GiB (10,000 parts of 32 MiB) when that isn't set. One fetch
may take up to 6 hours. A fetch that fails for a passing reason (a network error,
or a `5xx`, `408` or `429` answer) is tried 3 times in all, with a growing
wait between tries.

An import that fails for good ends the video `errored`, sends
`video.asset.errored`, and sets `error_code`:

| `error_code` | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| `import_url_refused` | The URL, or an address it redirected to, is not public. |
| `import_failed` | The fetch kept failing, or the server answered something other than `200`, or an empty body. |
| `import_too_large` | The file is larger than the import limit. |

A file that arrives but isn't a video ClipMux can read fails later, at
encoding, like an upload would.

## Check it works

Get the video until it's ready:

```bash
curl -s https://video.example.com/v1/assets/ast_… \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLIPMUX_API_KEY" | jq '{status, error_code}'
```

`processing` turns into `ready`. If it ends `errored`, `error_code` is one of
those above. For `import_failed`, fetch the URL yourself with
`curl -I` from somewhere outside your network: it must answer `200`.
